display.purpose: The hero name in expanded caps; the same treatment, fitted to its column, sets the loader name, contact headline and chapter titles.

headline.purpose: Section titles such as Toolbox and More work.

title.purpose: Index headings, preview titles, lead entries and case-study subheads.

index-row.purpose: World names in the index at normal width; the committed row widens to 125% and 700.

tagline.purpose: Chapter, case-study and lead-entry taglines at semi-wide width.

body-lg.purpose: Hero lede and other short lead paragraphs, max 34-60ch.

label.purpose: Nav, buttons, text links, readouts, numbers and facts. Never prose.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: Instrument surfaces carry no elevation shadows; depth is line weight and tonal steps of the print.

shadows.name: label-halo
shadows.value: paint-order: stroke; stroke: var(--cy-700); stroke-width: 6px; stroke-linejoin: round
shadows.purpose: Ground-colour halo behind orrery labels so crossing labels stay legible.

shadows.name: hairline-mount
shadows.purpose: Scene frame mount; offset tightens to 2px on hover.

shadows.name: focus
shadows.purpose: Focus ring on the blue; Cyanotype Lit on the sheet.

shadows.name: paper-grain
shadows.purpose: Watercolour-stock fibre over the whole page.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default for arrivals, floods, underline draws and settles. Nothing overshoots.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Symmetric moves such as curtains and scrubbed transitions.

motion.name: dur-hover
motion.purpose: Colour and underline changes on hover.

motion.name: dur-ui
motion.purpose: Row floods, nav underline, halos, nav hide.

motion.name: dur-arrival
motion.purpose: Body recolours, role slot width and contact letter rolls.

motion.name: orbital
motion.value: scroll- and drag-coupled rotation with velocity carry (springs at stiffness 70, damping 16)
motion.purpose: The orrery and contact moon: continuous, velocity-coupled, settling.

narrative.overview:
The site is one working instrument printed as a sun print: Prussian blue where light hit the paper, white where it did not. Samudra sits at the centre as the SK monogram sun; the projects are enamel bodies on dashed elliptical rings, and scrolling or dragging turns the whole mechanism. Everything on the blue is drawn as white engraved linework, so hierarchy comes from type size, type width and line weight rather than from boxes, fills or elevation.

Density is low and deliberate. Long blue passages (hero, worlds index, toolbox, more work) are broken by one quiet material, the unexposed white sheet, which carries About and the case-study bodies in blue ink. The seven project worlds are the loud exception: each keeps its own visual kit and palette, mounted inside the instrument on a hairline frame and never repainted by it.

Motion is orbital: continuous, velocity-coupled, settling on a long ease-out. Nothing overshoots or bounces, and every pin, scrub and smooth-scroll falls back to a static stacked layout under reduced motion.
keyCharacteristics: Drenched cyanotype blue ground, never black; the white sheet for quiet passages.
White hairline engraving: dashed means available, solid means committed.
One signal colour (lime) for conjunction, active state, focus and selection.
Archivo across its width axis: expanded caps display, normal-width reading; JetBrains Mono only for readouts.
No drop shadows and no rounded tiles; circles are the only curved form.
Project bodies carry each project's own enamel palette.

rules.name: The Never-Black Rule
rules.body: The instrument's darkest value is Cyanotype Deep. Pure or near-black grounds belong only to a project world's own kit.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Lime marks what is current or focused: the conjunction, the active link, the selection. It is never decoration and never a section background.

rules.name: The Enamel Rule
rules.body: A project's body, index-row flood, chapter, case study and transition curtain take that project's own palette. The instrument frames the worlds and never repaints them.

rules.name: The Width Axis Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from size and width together: wide caps for anything that names, normal width for anything that reads. Display titles are never set in a different family.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Measurement Rule
rules.body: Mono is for readouts, numbers, labels and controls. It never sets a sentence of prose.

rules.name: The Fitted Title Rule
rules.body: Long display titles are sized from their container and longest word (container-query units), so wide caps never spill under a scene or clip on a phone.

rules.name: The Line-Weight Depth Rule
rules.body: On instrument surfaces, a thing becomes more important by getting a heavier or solid line, a lime halo, or a wider typeface; never by gaining a shadow.

rules.name: The Dashed-Available, Solid-Committed Rule
rules.body: An available orbit, row disc or toolbox body is a dashed hairline. Once committed (in conjunction, hovered, focused, selected) it becomes solid and takes its enamel fill.

dos: Do print every instrument surface on the cyanotype ramp, from Cyanotype Deep to Cyanotype Exposed, and put quiet long-form passages on the Sheet in Sheet Ink.
Do draw structure as hairlines: `hairline` at rest, `hairline-strong` for orbits and rims, 1px rules between list rows.
Do use dashed for available and solid for committed, on orbits, discs and toolbox bodies alike.
Do keep lime for the current, focused or selected thing only.
Do set names and titles in Archivo at wide width (125%) and reading text at normal width; use JetBrains Mono only for labels, readouts and controls.
Do give every project body, flood, chapter and curtain that project's own palette.
Do keep targets at 44px or more and give every pinned or scrubbed sequence a static stacked fallback for reduced motion and screens under 1000px.
Do draw icons and arrows as inline stroked SVG, as the contact arrow does.
donts: Don't use drop shadows or offset shadows on instrument surfaces; depth is line weight and tone. (Project worlds keep their own kits.)
Don't round corners on buttons, rows, frames or objects; the circle is reserved for bodies.
Don't use black or near-black as an instrument ground; the darkest value is Cyanotype Deep.
Don't wrap content in cards on the blue; separate with type size and hairline rules.
Don't set prose in mono or titles in any face other than Archivo.
Don't let the orrery bleed or clip on compact screens; it stays whole on the page.
Don't repaint a project world in the instrument's colours.
